blocks.text: The **Mughal Empire (1526–1857)**, founded by **Babur** at Panipat, was medieval India's grandest state. The **Great Mughals — Babur, Humayun, Akbar, Jahangir, Shah Jahan, Aurangzeb** — built and expanded it to near-subcontinental extent before its 18th-century decline.

**2nd Panipat (1556)** vs Hemu; mansabdari; **Din-i-Ilahi**; Rajput policy; abolished jizya.
Nur Jahan; captured Kangra; execution of Guru Arjan; Captain Hawkins/Sir Thomas Roe.
**Taj Mahal**; golden age of architecture; Deccan wars.
Greatest extent; re-imposed **jizya (1679)**; 27-yr Deccan/Maratha war; empire overstretched.

'Alamgir'; re-imposed **Jizya (1679)**; executed Guru Tegh Bahadur & Sambhaji; Deccan/Maratha wars drained the empire; Fatawa-i-Alamgiri.

blocks.text: The Mughals ran India's most **integrated pre-modern administration** — the **mansabdari service, Todar Mal's revenue settlement, and a provincial pyramid** — funding a **prosperous, monetised, trade-rich economy**; **Akbar's** liberal reforms are its high point.

rows: **Akbar's** ranking by **zat (status) & sawar (cavalry)**; transferable, salaried nobility; paid via **jagir**.
**Todar Mal's** system — measured land, classified soil, cash demand on a 10-year average (~1/3).
**Subah → Sarkar → Pargana → village**; Subedar, Diwan, Faujdar.
Abolished jizya (1564) & pilgrim tax; **Sulh-i-kul, Ibadat Khana, Din-i-Ilahi, Mansabdari, Rajput alliances**.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: Mughal administration & economy

items: **Mansabdari (Akbar)**: every officer held a dual rank — **Zat** (personal status/pay) & **Sawar** (cavalry to maintain); paid in cash or via **Jagir** (revenue assignment); nobility multi-ethnic (Turani, Irani, Rajput, Indian Muslim).

**Land revenue — Zabti/Dahsala (Todar Mal, 1580)**: measured land (bigha), classified soil (Polaj, Parauti, Chachar, Banjar), fixed state share (**~1/3**) on a **10-year average** in cash; other systems — Ghalla-Bakhshi (crop-sharing), Nasaq, Kankut.

**Central offices**: **Wazir/Diwan** (revenue), **Mir Bakhshi** (military/mansab), **Khan-i-Saman** (household), **Sadr-us-Sudur** (religious/charity), **Qazi** (justice); provinces = **Subah (Subedar) → Sarkar → Pargana → village**; **Faujdar** (law-order), **Amil/Amalguzar** (revenue), **Kotwal** (city).

**Economy**: agrarian surplus, monetised silver **rupiya** economy, vibrant **textile exports** (Bengal muslin, Gujarat), **karkhanas** (royal workshops), Indian Ocean trade via Surat; but the **jagirdari-mansabdari crisis** (be-jagiri) contributed to decline.
Mansabdari (zat & sawar) + Todar Mal's Zabti revenue = the two pillars to always cite.
Akbar's liberal policy (jizya abolished, Sulh-i-kul, Din-i-Ilahi) is the analytical core.

blocks.text: The Mughals raised **Indo-Islamic art to its zenith** — the **Taj Mahal and Fatehpur Sikri, the Mughal miniature school, Persian and translated literature** — a **Ganga-Jamuni synthesis** that peaked under Shah Jahan.

rows: **Fatehpur Sikri (Buland Darwaza, Panch Mahal), Agra Fort, Humayun's Tomb** (predecessor of the Taj).
**Taj Mahal, Red Fort, Jama Masjid, Moti Masjid**; **pietra dura, charbagh, bulbous dome**; the marble golden age.
**Mughal miniature** (Persian Safavid + Indian) — peak under **Jahangir**; artists Mansur, Bishandas.
**Persian** (court language); **Baburnama, Akbarnama/Ain (Abul Fazl), Jahangir's Tuzuk**; Sanskrit translations (Mahabharata → Razmnama).

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: Mughal art, architecture & letters

items: **Architecture**: synthesis of **Persian + Indian**; **charbagh** gardens, bulbous domes, pietra dura, red sandstone→marble. **Humayun's Tomb** (first garden-tomb, **UNESCO**), **Fatehpur Sikri** (Buland Darwaza, Panch Mahal, Salim Chishti tomb — Akbar), **Taj Mahal, Red Fort, Jama Masjid** (Shah Jahan — zenith), **Bibi-ka-Maqbara** (Aurangzeb — 'Deccan Taj').

**Painting**: **Mughal miniature** school peaked under **Jahangir** (Ustad Mansur — flora/fauna; Abul Hasan; portraiture & naturalism); declined under Aurangzeb → artists dispersed → **Rajput/Pahari (Kangra, Basohli)** schools.

**Literature & history**: **Abul Fazl** (**Ain-i-Akbari & Akbarnama**), **Badauni**, **Abdul Rahim Khan-i-Khana** (Hindi dohas), **Tulsidas & Surdas** (Bhakti — contemporary); Persian as court language; translation bureau (**Maktab Khana** — Ramayana/Mahabharata into Persian).
**Music**: **Tansen** (Akbar's navratna); Dhrupad flourished.
Akbar = Fatehpur Sikri/Humayun's tomb (charbagh, red sandstone); Shah Jahan = Taj/marble/pietra dura.
Miniature painting peaked under Jahangir (Mansur — nature studies).

blocks.text: The **Bhakti Movement** was a **devotional reform current (7th–17th c.)** stressing **loving devotion to a personal god, equality, and vernacular worship** over ritual and caste. Beginning with the Tamil **Alvars and Nayanars**, it spread across India through **saguna and nirguna** saints, democratising religion and enriching vernacular literature.

rows: Tamil; **Vishnu (Alvars) & Shiva (Nayanars)** devotion — the earliest Bhakti (7th-10th c.).
**Namdev, Tukaram, Ramdas (Maharashtra); Shankaradeva (Assam)**; in Andhra — **Annamayya, Ramadasu, Vemana, Potana**.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: the Bhakti Movement

items: **Origin**: began with the Tamil **Alvars (Vishnu)** & **Nayanars (Shiva)** (6th–9th c); philosophically systematised by the **acharyas** — **Shankara (Advaita/monism, 8th c), Ramanuja (Vishishtadvaita), Madhva (Dvaita), Nimbarka, Vallabha**.
**Two streams**: **Saguna** (God with form — Rama/Krishna: **Tulsidas, Surdas, Mirabai, Chaitanya, Vallabha**) & **Nirguna** (formless — **Kabir, Guru Nanak, Dadu, Ravidas**).

**Major saints**: **Ramananda** (north, taught in Hindi, disciples across castes), **Kabir** (weaver; dohas; Hindu-Muslim synthesis), **Guru Nanak** (founded **Sikhism**), **Chaitanya** (Bengal, Krishna-Gaudiya), **Mirabai** (Rajasthan), **Namdev & Tukaram & Jnaneshwar** (Maharashtra Varkari), **Shankaradeva** (Assam), **Ramanuja** & the Alvars (south).

**Ideas & impact**: **monotheism, devotion over ritual, equality/anti-caste, vernacular languages, guru-bhakti, social reform**; enriched regional literatures; fostered Hindu-Muslim harmony; but did not abolish caste structurally.

blocks.text: Prelims mapping: **Alvars→Vishnu, Nayanars→Shiva**; **Kabir/Nanak = Nirguna**, **Tulsi/Sur/Mira/Chaitanya = Saguna**; **Shankara=Advaita, Ramanuja=Vishishtadvaita, Madhva=Dvaita**.

items: Distinguish Saguna (Tulsidas, Surdas, Mira, Chaitanya) vs Nirguna (Kabir, Nanak, Ramananda).
Alvars/Nayanars = earliest (Tamil); impact = vernacular growth, social equality, Hindu-Muslim synthesis.

blocks.text: **Sufism** — Islamic **mysticism** seeking union with God through **love, devotion and self-purification** — spread across India via **silsilas (orders)**, above all the **Chishti and Suhrawardi**. Its **khanqahs, tolerance and vernacular devotion (qawwali)** paralleled the Bhakti movement and fostered **Hindu-Muslim synthesis**.

rows: **Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti (Ajmer)** — founder in India; **Nizamuddin Auliya (Delhi), Baba Farid, Salim Chishti**; simple, tolerant, sama (music).
**Bahauddin Zakariya (Multan)** — accepted state patronage & wealth (unlike Chishtis).
**Wahdat-ul-Wujud (unity of being — Ibn Arabi)**, love (ishq), pir-murid (master-disciple), khanqah.
**Qawwali (Amir Khusrau), Urdu, Hindu-Muslim harmony, vernacular poetry**.

items: **Sufism** = Islamic mysticism seeking union with God via love; organised into **silsilas (orders)** centred on **Khanqahs** (hospices) led by a **Pir/Shaikh** with **murids** (disciples); practices — **Zikr, Sama (music/qawwali), Wahdat-ul-Wujud** (unity of being).

**Chishti order** (most influential, India-rooted, kept distance from the state): **Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti (Ajmer)**, **Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki (Delhi)**, **Baba Farid (Punjab)**, **Nizamuddin Auliya (Delhi)** & disciple **Amir Khusrau**, **Nasiruddin Chirag-i-Dilli**, **Bandanawaz Gesudaraz (Gulbarga)**.

**Suhrawardi order** (accepted state office/wealth): Bahauddin Zakariya (Multan); **Qadiri** (Mian Mir), **Naqshbandi** (orthodox — Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi opposed Akbar's liberalism), **Firdausi** (Sharfuddin Yahya Maneri).

**Impact**: fostered **Hindu-Muslim harmony & Bhakti-Sufi synthesis** (Kabir), popularised **Urdu/Hindavi & qawwali**, gave the masses an accessible, egalitarian devotion; dargahs remain shared pilgrimage centres.
Chishti (Ajmer, tolerant, no state patronage) vs Suhrawardi (Multan, accepted wealth/state) is the key contrast.
Wahdat-ul-Wujud, khanqah, sama (qawwali) and Hindu-Muslim synthesis = the influence.

prelimsPointers: **Chishti order** — introduced by **Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti (dargah at Ajmer)**; avoided state patronage.
**Nizamuddin Auliya** (Delhi) — greatest Chishti; disciple **Amir Khusrau**.
**Suhrawardi order** — **Bahauddin Zakariya (Multan)**; accepted royal patronage & wealth.
**Wahdat-ul-Wujud** ('unity of being') — Sufi doctrine (Ibn Arabi).

**Naqshbandi** order — **Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi** led an orthodox reaction against syncretism.
Influence — **qawwali, Urdu, vernacular devotional poetry, Hindu-Muslim synthesis**.
**Chishti** order (Ajmer's **Moinuddin Chishti**, Delhi's **Nizamuddin Auliya**) = most influential, aloof from state.
**Suhrawardi** (Multan, Bahauddin Zakariya) accepted state patronage; **Naqshbandi** = orthodox (Sirhindi v Akbar).
Concepts: **Zikr, Sama, Wahdat-ul-Wujud**; hospice = **Khanqah**, master = **Pir/Shaikh**.
**Amir Khusrau** was Nizamuddin Auliya's disciple; Sufism ↔ Bhakti synthesis (Kabir).
